ai.title: catch checkToAllowUnboundedIteration errors defaulting to false
ai.summary: checkToAllowUnboundedIteration now catches errors and returns false. Unhandled exceptions previously crashed mainPrompt. Scope limited to backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Error logging added via logger.error.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to answer a follow-up question in a long conversation, it occasionally runs into a behind-the-scenes glitch that used to cause the whole session to crash. Now, if that glitch occurs, the assistant quietly treats that step as 'not needed' and keeps going instead of failing altogether. You won't see a specific error message, but conversations that previously stopped mid-way should now continue more smoothly. This is a small stability fix that only affects how those particular follow-up questions are handled.

ai.title: Remove troubleshooting guide, add codebuff dependency
ai.summary: Deleted `web/src/content/help/troubleshooting.mdx` and added `codebuff` (^1.0.119) to `package.json` dependencies. Dev dependencies were alphabetized and reordered. Scope limited to repo metadata and web content directory.

eli5.text: The troubleshooting guide page has been removed from the website, so visitors looking for step-by-step help with common problems like connection issues or permission errors will no longer find that dedicated page. The software now includes a new tool called Codebuff as part of its core setup, which was added alongside some behind-the-scenes reordering of development packages. If you browsed the site today, you'd notice the missing help page and the updated package, but the overall experience remains unchanged for most users.

ai.title: Rewrite Benjamin Bryant case study
ai.summary: Condensed `web/src/content/case-studies/benjamin-bryant.mdx` to a concise narrative focusing on speed gains and Codebuff's pattern matching. Removed verbose sections on learning curves, iteration processes, and specific anecdotes about multi-repo workflows or Finbarr. Scope limited to the web content directory.

eli5.text: The Benjamin Bryant story on the company's website got shorter. If you go to that case study page now, you'll read about how Benjamin uses the AI coding tool to save time on his work, with a direct quote about it being like an extension of his brain, but the long details about his investment fund's daily routine and the technical challenges of setting it up are gone. This only affects what visitors see on that one web page.

ai.title: Add docs news feed, lower sponsee names
ai.summary: Adds a docs News section backed by new `web/src/app/api/feed/route.ts`, which fetches `https://news.codebuff.com/feed` and regex-parses feed items into JSON articles. `web/src/lib/docs.ts` exposes `getNewsArticles()` for `web/src/components/docs/doc-sidebar.tsx`, while `web/src/app/[sponsee]/page.tsx` lowercases `params['sponsee']`, `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` logs failed unbounded-iteration checks and returns false, and `package.json` adds `codebuff` `^1.0.119`. Scope covers the Web docs sidebar/footer, sponsee page, backend prompt flow, package metadata, and removes `web/src/content/help/troubleshooting.mdx`. The feed route returns HTTP 500 when the upstream fetch fails.

eli5.text: The documentation sidebar on the company website now includes a News section that automatically displays the latest articles from https://news.codebuff.com/feed. Sponsee profile pages (accessed via URLs like /some-sponsee) now render consistently regardless of whether the sponsee name in the URL is typed in upper or lower case. The backend assistant flow now logs errors and defaults to non-unbounded iteration when checks fail, improving reliability. Additionally, the troubleshooting guide has been removed, and the codebuff dependency has been updated to version 1.0.119.

ai.title: Rename Mode to CostMode
ai.summary: Renamed `Mode` to `CostMode` across backend and CLI. Updated `getModelForMode` to handle new 'check-new-files' operation with GPT-4o. Refactored imports and type definitions in `common/constants.ts`, `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, and `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Ensures consistent naming for cost-based model selection logic.

eli5.text: The system has been updated to use clearer naming for its cost-based model selection. Previously, a core concept was called 'Mode', which has been renamed to 'CostMode' to make it more obvious that the setting relates to how much the service costs to run. For example, a 'cheap' mode means the system will choose a faster, less expensive AI model, while an 'expensive' mode means it will use a more powerful, more costly model. Users won't see a direct change in how the service works, but the underlying logic for deciding which AI model to use for different tasks (like processing agent actions or checking for new files) has been made more readable and consistent behind the scenes.

ai.title: Refactor testimonials into smaller cards
ai.summary: Replaced generic Card components with a custom ReviewCard in web/src/app/page.tsx. Updated web/src/lib/testimonials.ts to adjust author casing and reorder entries. This change reduces visual weight and standardizes testimonial display.

eli5.text: The testimonials shown on the main page now appear in smaller, more uniform cards instead of larger generic ones. If you clicked through to the site, you'd notice each review has a tighter layout with the author's name, title, and a short quote displayed consistently. The order of testimonials was shuffled, and one author's name was changed from 'Anonymous' to lowercase 'anonymous' for stylistic consistency. This is a behind-the-scenes housekeeping update with no new functionality.

ai.title: Rename cost modes lite and pro
ai.summary: Cost mode identifiers renamed from 'cheap'/'expensive' to 'lite'/'pro' across core constants, CLI flags, and backend logic. Updates apply to `common/src/constants.ts`, `npm-app/src/index.ts`, and `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`. CLI now accepts `--lite` and `--pro` flags instead of `--cheap` and `--expensive`. Welcome messages in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` reflect the new mode names.

eli5.text: You can now tell the assistant to work in a lighter, cheaper way or a heavier, more powerful way by saying 'lite' or 'pro' instead of the old 'cheap' or 'expensive', those names were confusing, so they were changed. When you start a session, the welcome message will also show which mode you’re in, like “Welcome back Alex (pro mode)!”. The switch happened behind the scenes across the assistant’s settings and commands, so everything you type or see now uses the new names automatically.

ai.title: CLI startup mode indicator
ai.summary: The CLI startup sequence in `npm-app/src/index.ts` now displays the active `costMode` using colored text before the working directory prompt. `npm-app/src/cli.ts` no longer includes mode descriptions in the welcome message. The `start` script in `npm-app/package.json` was simplified to remove an explicit build step.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it now tells you in color whether you're in Lite mode (yellow) or Pro mode (blue) right at the top, before it shows you the folder it's working in. The startup message that used to mention your mode when welcoming you back has been removed, so the mode is only shown once, upfront. The system also no longer runs a separate build step when starting up, which makes launching a bit simpler behind the scenes. This is live today for anyone who runs the tool locally.

ai.title: Cost mode selection added to agent operations
ai.summary: New `costMode` parameter ('lite', 'normal', 'pro') propagates from WebSocket `user-input` action through `mainPrompt` and `requestRelevantFiles` to `promptClaudeStream` and `promptClaude`. `getModelForMode` in `common/src/constants.ts` selects between `claudeModels.haiku` and `claudeModels.sonnet` for agent operations, and `claudeModels.sonnet` vs `claudeModels.opus` for file-requests/check-new-files based on mode. `requestRelevantFiles` adjusts `countPerRequest` (5/6/7) and skips `examplePromise`/`newFilesNecessaryPromise` in 'lite' mode. `CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA` in `common/src/actions.ts` adds optional `costMode` enum defaulting to 'normal'.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant, nothing changes for you right now - the tool you run just got a new version number so the team can tell which release you're on. Behind the scenes, the software switched to a faster startup engine (Bun), added support for Google's Gemini model alongside the existing one, and let you pick between a cheaper or more thorough mode with simple switches instead of typing a mode name. A few small fixes landed too: it now handles a couple of error cases more gracefully and the CLI shows which mode it started in. Since these pieces are still being wired together, you won't notice their effects until the next time you update.

ai.title: Document --lite and --pro cost mode flags
ai.summary: Adds documentation for the `--lite` and `--pro` CLI flags across README, help docs, and startup menus. Updates `npm-app/src/index.ts` to fix spacing in mode announcement strings. Covers `npm-app/README.md`, `web/src/content/help/getting-started.mdx`, and `web/src/content/help/keyboard-shortcuts.mdx`.

eli5.text: When you start Codebuff, you can now tell it to spend less or spend more by typing --lite (cheaper, simpler answers) or --pro (pricier, deeper answers). Codebuff will also remind you that these options exist in its welcome message and in the on-screen help menu. This is purely documentation, so nothing about how --lite or --pro work changed, just that they are now explained in more places.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.121
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.121 in npm-app/package.json. No functional changes. Scope limited to package metadata.

eli5.text: If you install or update the assistant today, you can now see what the --lite and --pro cost options do in the help screens, startup menus, and written instructions. These are menu and documentation labels that explain two ways to control how much the assistant is allowed to spend during a task. Updating brings those labels and explanations to your copy; the spending choices themselves were already available.

The layout was adjusted so the main text now sits centered and code examples scroll horizontally when they don't fit, FAQ sections have a little extra breathing room on the sides, and a few navigation tweaks made the Docs link easier to reach. If you open the site on a small device today, pages that previously required zooming or horizontal panning now display cleanly without anything getting cut off.

The layout was adjusted so the sidebar and main content sit at fixed widths with consistent spacing, keeping everything aligned and balanced on larger screens. This fix is live now and affects anyone viewing the internal docs on a desktop or laptop.
